title: Policy Service Manual — Reinstatement Filings on the Cardinal Financial Responsibility Filing
content:
## Section

When the certified Cardinal Personal Auto Policy is reinstated, a reinstatement filing restores each Cardinal Financial Responsibility Filing certificate on it that is still cancel-notified — that is, an SR-26 cancellation notice has been transmitted for it and has not yet taken effect. The reinstatement filing returns the certificate to accepted.

Retired wording: the clause "carrying the reinstatement filing fee", formerly attached to the reinstatement filing, is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current charge basis for reinstatement filings.

## Timing

A reinstatement filing is made only when the policy is reinstated before the SR-26 effective date of the filing. The SR-26 effective date on the filing record is the boundary, and a reinstatement on that date or later is too late.

- The record that decides is the SR-26 effective date shown on that filing's record, not a date the customer gives.
- The comparison is strict: the reinstatement must fall on a day earlier than the SR-26 effective date.

A certificate that has already lapsed is not reinstated; a new filing is requested instead.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical dates)

| SR-26 effective date on the filing record | Policy reinstated | Reinstatement filing? |
|---|---|---|
| 20 March | 19 March | Yes — before the effective date |
| 20 March | 20 March | No — on the effective date is too late |
| 20 March | 22 March | No — the certificate lapsed; a new filing is requested instead |

## Questions answered

**Two filings on one policy, both cancel-notified, and the policy is reinstated in time for both?** Each is restored by a reinstatement filing.

**The policy is reinstated, but the certificate already shows lapsed?** It is not reinstated; a new filing is requested.
